contexts.text: Stringed instruments and singing, in worship, represented (the spiritual things of faith). Hence there were so many singers, and musicians; and this because all heavenly joy produces gladness of heart, which was testified by singing, and then by stringed instruments which emulated and exalted the singing. Every affection of the heart... produces singing, consequently the things of singing. The affection of the heart is celestial; the consequent singing is spiritual.

That singing and what is like it = what is spiritual, has been evident to me from the angelic choirs, which are of two kinds: celestial, and spiritual. Spiritual choirs, from their vibratory singing tone, to which the sound of stringed instruments may be likened, are very different from the celestial. Moreover the Most Ancients referred what is spiritual to the province of the lungs, thus something spiritual to everything of the lungs, as the singing voice, and things like it, thus to the tones of such instruments.
To sing in the Word, = what is spiritual. Illustrated.
Their voice shall sing in the windows () = reasonings from phantasies. See AC 3391:2.
Such was the form of songs anciently. Explained.
Under Speak, see this reference.
There is heard from (the angelic Spirits) as from afar, a sweetly modulating sound, as it were of singing.
Not to drink wine in the song () = not to be instructed from the affection of truth. AE 376:20.
Voice of singing, etc. = what is spiritual. Illustrated.

The celebration (of the Lord by the angelic choirs) was sometimes heard as from sweet singing... but human singing is not to be compared to (angelic) for sweetness and harmony... The choirs belonged to the province of the lungs... because singing is the office of the lungs.
Song is a spiritual expression.
I would have sent thee away with... songs () = ... a state as to truths... for songs are predicated of truths.
Gladness of mind, and joy of mind, produce (by correspondence) singing and joyful shouting.
To come with singing () = the gladness of the affection of truth.
The singers () re predicated of the truths which are of the Spiritual Church.
The tongue of the dumb shall Sing () = that these will confess the Lord, and the things which are of faith in Him.
In all angelic discourse there is a harmony like that of songs.
These are the things contained in this prophetic song.
Then sang Moses and the sons of Israel this song to Jehovah () = a Glorification of the Lord by those of the Spiritual Church on account of deliverance... To sing a song = a Glorification.

The reason to sing a song = to Glorify, and a song, Glorification, is that the songs in the Ancient and Jewish Churches were prophetic, and treated of the Lord, especially that He should come into the world, and destroy the diabolical crew... and deliver the faithful... Hence the songs signified the Glorification of the Lord, that is, the celebration of Him from gladness of heart; for gladness of heart is especially expressed by a song; for in a song gladness as it were of itself breaks forth into sound. Hence in the songs the Lord is called a Hero, etc.

The Angels with the men were at the same time in the Glorification of the Lord; hence those who sang, and those who heard the songs, had heavenly gladness... in which they seemed to themselves to be as it were carried up into Heaven. Such an effect had the songs of the Church among the Ancients; such an effect they might have at this day also; for the spiritual Angels are especially affected by songs concerning the Lord, His kingdom, and Church. The reason the songs of the Church had this effect, was not only from the fact that gladness of heart was made active by them, and that it broke forth from the interior even to the extreme fibres of the body, moving these with a glad and at the same time a holy tremor; but also because the Glorification of the Lord in the Heavens is effected by choirs, and thus by the harmony of many.
Hence the Glorifications of the Lord, among the Ancients of the Church, were performed by songs, psalms, and musical instruments...
That the prophetical songs contained, in the internal sense, the Glorification of the Lord. Illustrated.

(Thus) a song = the Glorification of the Lord for deliverance; for the songs involved gladness of heart, and the exaltation of the Lord; gladness of heart for the Lord's advent, and Salvation then; and exaltation for victory over spiritual enemies. Gladness of heart attended with the exaltation of the Lord, is what is meant by Glorification.
That gladness of heart was signified by songs. Illustrated.
That the exaltation of the Lord was effected by songs. Illustrated.
The song of Moses and of the Lamb () is the song contained in this chapter. It is called the song of the Lamb because it treats of the Glorification of the Lord.
I will sing to Jehovah () = that glory belongs to the Lord alone. AC 8341.

My song is Jah () = that everything of faith and thence of glory is from the Divine truth which is from Him; for a song, when said concerning Jehovah, = the Glorification of the Lord; but when concerning man, as here, it = the glory which is from faith, thus the faith from which is glory. Explained.
A song = the faith which is of Divine truth.
To Sing = to Glorify.
(Antiphonal singing. See Choir.)
(Effect of the singing of a Psalm upon Spirits and Angels. See Psalm.)
Like one who sings only one note on his pipe.
(Thus) mere changes and variations, successively continued, of the state of the organic forms, produce tones and their articulations, which are speech and singing.

They sang a new song () = the acknowledgement and Glorification of the Lord: that He alone is the Judge, the Redeemer, and Saviour; thus the God of Heaven and earth. These things are contained in the song which they sang. Enumerated... Hence it is called a new song. AE 326.

The reason a song = Glorification, which is confession from joy of heart, is that singing exalts, and causes the affection to break forth from the heart into sound, and to present itself intensely in its life.
The Psalms of David are nothing but songs... Illustrated.
That the songs were for the sake of the exaltation of the life of love, and the derivative joy. Illustrated.

They sang as it were a new song () = the celebration and Glorification of the Lord in the New Christian Heaven; here, in special, that He is acknowledged as the God of Heaven and earth, as He is acknowledged in the ancient Heavens. AE 857.

No one could learn that song but the 144,000 () = that none from Christians could understand (this) except those received into this New Heaven. This song = the acknowledgement and Glorification of the Lord, that He is the God of Heaven and earth. AE 859.

They sang the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb () = confession from charity, and thus from a life according to the commandments, and from faith in the Divinity of the Lord's Human. Explained. AE 936.
In Heaven there are... songs in the greatest perfection...
At the sides there are Singers and Songstresses, who entertain the citizens with most pleasant solos and part songs...

Every morning, from the houses round the public places are heard the sweetest songs of virgins and girls, with which the whole city resounds. One affection of spiritual love is sung each morning, that is, is sounded by modifications of the singing voice, or by modulations; and that affection in the song is perceived as if it were [the affection] itself; it inflows into the souls of the hearers, and excites them to correspondence. Such is heavenly singing. The songstresses say that the sound of their song as it were breathes itself in and animates from within, and exalts delightfully according to the reception by the hearers. CL 19.

A very sweet strain heard from Heaven: wives and virgins were singing a song. The sweetness of the singing was like the affection of some love flowing forth harmoniously. Heavenly songs are nothing else than sonorous affections, or affections expressed and modified in sounds; for as thoughts are expressed by speech, so are affections by songs. From the symmetry and flowing forth of the rhythmical measure, the Angels perceive the subject of the affection... They were singing the chaste love of the sex.
The song continued, and each of the bystanders heard it according to the state of his love. Enumerated.

[155a]. One morning very sweet singing... awoke me... The singing of Heaven is nothing else than an affection of the mind sent out from the mouth as a melody... I perceived it was the affection of the deliciousnesses of conjugial love which was made melodious by wives in Heaven. I observed this from the tone of the song, in which these deliciousnesses were varied in wonderful ways.
The virgins then sang an ode, in which they expressed the affection of works of use with its pleasantnesses, in an angelic strain.
See Psalm.

I have again heard them hymning or chanting the praise of our Saviour; some choirs together... without confusion; one within another. Thus is the universal Heaven wont to be in the praise and glory of the Saviour. Hence musical harmony and singing are so delicious to the Angels, when the thoughts of men are in accordance with their ideas; as I have often experienced in places of worship, in that the angelic choirs were in accordance, with an intonate perception of gladness, ineffable.

Two or three times I have heard harmonious singing... and the Spirits were so delighted with that singing that they became as it were spellbound. The sweetness penetrated their interiors. In like manner with the Angels.

Again have I heard a harmonious singing, and the harmony of it from the discords was carried by the Lord to the deliciousnesses of Spirits and Angels, who were so spell-bound with the mere deliciousnesses, that they said they did not know but that they had been translated into the inmost Heaven; even Spirits not good, so that they have been rapt out of themselves with the sweetness. I have not often perceived such a quiet; for they are in a delicious stupor. SE 2231, Further described. SE 2232.
(Like) evil Spirits lulled by singing.
Cantatum occurs.
(The birds) then begin to sing beautifully, from the quiet thence.
(In the other life) they have songs, and they sing from them exactly as here. The spiritual are very greatly delighted with songs.
The joy thence is described by, sing ye heavens, exult earth, and break forth into singing, mountains (). Explained. AE 405:9.
Singing = the testification of gladness from the affection of truth.
The good of truth is expressed by to Sing...
Vastation as to the Knowledges of good, is signified by, I will make the noise of thy songs to cease ().

A song = acknowledgement and confession from joy of heart... because joy of heart expresses itself by singing when it is in its fulness; and the reason this is done by singing, is that when the heart is full of joy, and derivatively the thought also, it then pours itself forth by singing; the joy itself of the heart, by the sound of the singing, and the derivative joy of the thought, by the song. The quality of the joy of the thought is presented by the words of the song... and the quality of the joy of the heart, by the harmony; and the quantity of its joy, by the uplifting of the sound and of the words in it. All these things flow as if spontaneously from the joy itself. Explained.
(Thus) the harmony of singing... is from the Spiritual World, and not from the natural.

To (these instruments) was adjoined singing with songs, by means of which were formed accordances of Things with the tones of affections. All the Psalms of David were such, and therefore they are called (also) songs. AE 326:end, Illustrated.
That singing, and to sing a song = acknowledgement and confession from joy of heart. Fully illustrated.
Where the Lord's advent is treated of, a new song is mentioned. Illustrated.
They shall come to Zion with singing... () = eternal happiness.
To sing in the height of Zion () = internal heavenly joy...
In the vineyards no singing () = their delight taken away; for they were wont to sing in the vineyards and winepresses to represent delights from truths.
To sing a song, and to praise () = worship from a glad mind.
Shall Sing () = joy from the intelligence of truth.
Their joy from the preaching and Knowledge of truth, is signified by to sing praise, and to lift up the voice ().
He shall answer, that is, sing.
All spiritual gladness is from the affection of truth, and therefore to sing, etc., are said of virgins and girls.
Singing describes the gladness of those of the Spiritual Kingdom. Illustrated.
To praise with lips of singers () = to worship through truths which gladden the mind.
5. Sounds which derive little from the understanding are those of singing and music.
The correspondence of the variations of sound, as those of singing, etc., is with the variations of affections which are from the love of the will in the understanding.
